From 3.5.0 until 3.13.0, built-in penetration-detection patterns in guard_core/handlers/suspatterns_handler.py execute through a direct pattern.search(content) call instead of the timeout-protected create_safe_matcher() path used for custom patterns. The built-in template-injection detector contains an unbounded expression with quadratic behavior when scanning repeated opening braces. Because penetration detection and enhanced mode are enabled by a stock SecurityConfig, an unauthenticated request can block the shared asyncio event loop, affecting all application endpoints. The triggering input does not produce a detection match, so the request can complete without incrementing ban counters or being recorded as suspicious. This issue is fixed in version 3.13.0.

CVE-2026-133763.title: Sandbox `__toString()` policy bypass via the `is true` test
CVE-2026-133763.description:
The sandbox checks that a template may call toString() on an object before converting it to a string. For an object, the is true test evaluates to the object itself, and that result wasn't checked. A sandboxed template could therefore print an object through a denied toString() method:

{{ obj is true }}

The same applies when the result is concatenated or passed to a filter. No tag needs to be allowed. A test in a boolean context, like {% if obj is true %}, isn't affected, since it doesn't convert the object to a string.

The sandbox now checks the result of tests like the result of filters and functions.

CVE-2026-54039.title: LibreChat: Pre-registration account takeover via attacker-controlled `provider` field and social-login email fallback
CVE-2026-54039.description: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. From 0.7.0 until 0.8.6, when local registration is enabled and at least one social provider is configured, POST /api/auth/register passes an unparsed request object into api/server/services/AuthService.js, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to persist a forged provider value for a known victim email. The api/strategies/socialLogin.js email-fallback path then accepts the planted record when the victim signs in because it compares the stored provider name without requiring the provider subject identifier. The victim OAuth session and the attacker local-password session become bound to the same user record, giving the attacker persistent read and write access to data created by the victim. The first-user administrator role is an additional conditional impact only on a fresh deployment. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.6.

CVE-2026-81828.description: Server-Side Request Forgery in SurveyWrapper in Apache OFBiz 24.09 before 24.09.08 on all platforms allows an authenticated back-office user holding catalog permission to cause the server to fetch and render attacker-controlled URLs — including internal network and cloud-metadata endpoints and local files via file:// — by setting an arbitrary URL as a product-store survey's template location, causing SurveyWrapper.getTemplate to call URL.openStream() on the resolved location and compile the fetched content as a FreeMarker template with no scheme or host validation, unlike the sibling widget location-loaders (ScreenFactory, FormFactory, GridFactory, MenuFactory, TreeFactory, ThemeFactory) which validate the resolved location before loading it. The fetched content is rendered into the HTTP response of any shopper who subsequently loads the affected product-store survey, making the disclosure non-blind. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 24.09.08, which fixes this issue.

CVE-2026-83493.title: Distributed-workloads: github actions pinned by mutable tag/branch, including third-party snyk/actions/setup@master
CVE-2026-83493.description: A flaw was found in distributed-workloads. A remote attacker could exploit a vulnerability in the pull_request_target workflow by submitting a specially crafted pull request. This workflow processes untrusted code from the pull request author while operating with the base repository's sensitive secrets, such as the SNYK_TOKEN, and its default write token. Consequently, an attacker could exfiltrate these secrets, leading to unauthorized access to the Snyk integration and potential control over the repository.

CVE-2026-87040.description:

CVE-2026-99630.title: drm/amdgpu/userq: validate the moved individual BOs on restore
CVE-2026-99630.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu/userq: validate the moved individual BOs on restore

An individual BO of a user queue VM, i.e. one which doesn't share the
root reservation, goes to the individual needs_update list when it is
evicted. The user queue restore looked at vm->invalidated for them, which
the VM state machine rework turned into the always_valid evicted list and
commit 18decfc9e8cc ("drm/amdgpu/userq: actually validate userq BOs")
into the individual evicted one. That list only holds imported DMA-bufs of
compute VMs though, so for a user queue VM nothing is validated.

The restore then neither locks such a BO nor moves it back. Its PTEs are
updated to wherever it is now, cleared if it went to system memory, and
it doesn't get the new eviction fence, so it can move again under the
running queue.
